claims.claim: Bryce Lynch distinguishes detail, which he calls trivia, from specificity, and says detail is bad.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: In this context detail is bad. It is trivia.

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says one well written specific sentence is worth more than a page of details.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: one well written specific sentence is worth more

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch defines specificity as terse, so that it does not interrupt the DM scanning the page.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: It is terse, meaning it doesn’t get in the way

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says the specific sentence communicates to the DM exactly the vibe to aim for.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: It communicates exactly the vibe the DM should be going for.

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says a single parenthetical adjective on a random-encounter entry tells the DM a great deal.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: That (dubious) in parens tells us a lot.

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says quick adjectives and adverbs describing an NPC work where a paragraph of italic read-aloud for the same NPC fails.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: quick adjectives/adverbs used to describe NPCs hit so well

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch's verdict on exposition in an adventure text is that more is not better.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026

claims.claim: Justin Alexander rejects replacing borrowed material with generic versions, saying generic lacks identity.
claims.source: Justin Alexander, 'Ptolus: Running the Campaign - From Table to Page', The Alexandrian, 2018

claims.claim: Justin Alexander warns a writer adapting a home campaign against trying to recapture the campaign instead of the scenario.
claims.source: Justin Alexander, 'Ptolus: Running the Campaign - From Table to Page', The Alexandrian, 2018
claims.quote: trying to recapture the campaign instead of the scenario

claims.claim: Gus L says a game text made entirely of fruitful voids becomes at best a prose poem shaped like an instruction manual or gazetteer.
claims.source: Gus L, 'Maxims of the OSR', All Dead Generations, 2023
claims.quote: a mediocre at best prose poem in the form
claims.page: Maxims of the OSR, 'Roleplaying not Roll Playing'

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch praises a keying pattern in which each room opens with a short vibe overview before its bulleted details.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Lions of Tell Arn Part 2', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: The rooms start with a kind of vibe overview.
claims.page: Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 review

claims.claim: The room text Bryce Lynch holds up as the model is a string of verbless sensory noun phrases, quoted in his review.
claims.source: module text by Nikoline quoted in Bryce Lynch's review, tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.page: Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 review, quoted room 28

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch's test of a good room description is that it reads as if the writer had lived the room and got the mental image onto paper.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Lions of Tell Arn Part 2', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: someone called up a mental image in their head
claims.page: Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 review

claims.feature: other: transfer of an imagined place
claims.claim: Bryce Lynch states that transferring the writer's imagined room into the reading DM's head is the goal of good writing.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Lions of Tell Arn Part 2', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: That IS the goal of good writing.
claims.page: Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 review

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch praises bolding and italics used sparingly to draw the eye rather than overused.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Lions of Tell Arn Part 2', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: Bolding and italics are used to effect to draw the eye
claims.page: Lions of Tell Arn Part 2 review
